title: Queen of Puddings
subtitle: Baked custard, raspberry jam, and crisp meringue
excerpt: A Victorian British classic: a baked vanilla custard base enriched with breadcrumbs, spread with raspberry jam, and topped with a swirl of golden meringue. Three textures, one dish.

recipe.sourceNotes: Queen of Puddings is a Victorian British dessert that appears in recipe collections from the mid-nineteenth century. Mrs Beeton included a recipe in her 1861 Book of Household Management, and it is credited in some sources to the Royal kitchens of Charles II, though the earliest verified written recipe dates from about 1850. The pudding combines three textures in one dish: the firm, custardy breadcrumb base that sets in the oven; the sharp fruit jam layer; and the crisp, billowing meringue top. The breadcrumbs in the base absorb the custard as it bakes and give the pudding a denser, more substantial texture than a plain baked custard. It is classified as a frugal dish because it uses stale bread and a relatively small amount of egg.

content.text: Bake the custard base in a bain-marie (the roasting tin sitting in a larger tin of hot water) so it sets gently without curdling. Spread the jam over the custard while it is still slightly warm but fully set; if spread over a wet, liquid custard the jam will sink. The meringue should be piled high and returned to a hot oven for only 10 to 12 minutes so it browns on the outside but stays marshmallowy inside.

Heat the oven to 160 C (140 C fan). Warm the milk with the butter until the butter melts; do not boil. Stir in 75 g of the caster sugar, the vanilla, and the lemon zest. Whisk the 4 egg yolks lightly, then pour in the warm milk in a slow stream, whisking. Stir in the breadcrumbs.

Pour into a buttered 1.5-litre baking dish. Place the dish in a larger roasting tin and pour boiling water around it to come halfway up the sides. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until just set with a faint wobble in the centre. Remove from the water bath and leave to cool for 15 minutes.

Spread the jam evenly over the set custard. Whisk the 4 egg whites to stiff peaks. Gradually whisk in the 100 g of caster sugar, a tablespoon at a time, until the meringue is thick, glossy, and holds firm peaks. Pile on top of the jam layer.
Raise the oven temperature to 190 C (170 C fan). Bake for 10 to 12 minutes until the meringue is golden on the tips and peaks. Serve warm, not hot.
